abstract: We introduce StreamEval with four key features: 1 First interactive streaming video generation benchmark. 2 Fully open source. Benchmark data, evaluation code, protocols, and scoring rules are publicly available. 3 Comprehensive coverage. Five tasks cover avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing, with 300 scripted cases lasting 15 to 300 seconds. Ten metrics assess task execution, state consistency, visual fidelity, and audiovisual coordination. 4 Monthly updates. We will evaluate new and updated models and publish leaderboard results monthly. Results from 38 models show that high visual quality and identity retention do not necessarily coincide with reliable request execution or sustained state consistency. The leaderboard is available at https://streameval.ai.

sections.body: Existing benchmarks cover visual quality, multi-turn control, world editing or dialogue, but not avatar interaction, world generation and real-time video editing in one protocol. StreamEval contains 300 scripted cases of 15 to 300 s across five tasks. Each case has timed user requests and explicit criteria for what should change and what should be preserved. Ten metrics cover task execution, state consistency, visual fidelity and audiovisual coordination. The authors evaluate 38 models. Vidu S2 Avatar has the highest reported Dialogue score, and JoyAI-Video-Edit has the highest Preservation score in instruction editing.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: StreamEval introduces a 300-case benchmark spanning five interactive streaming video tasks with ten metrics.

sections.body: Qwen3.8-Max drafts session goals, timed controls and expected outcomes. An authored oracle then specifies what to establish, retain, cancel or restore at each checkpoint, and media inputs are screened against these requirements. Generated speech must reach a normalized word-error rate of at most 0.25 against the authored transcript. Judges are calibrated to at most 5% false positives, 10% false negatives and 10% unresolved decisions per class. The benchmark has 60 cases per task, with 12 at each of five durations, and the cases contain 1,347 planned online events. The authors state that dialogue and performance tasks do not test perception of a live user video stream.
sections.heading: The StreamEval Benchmark
sections.headline: Each case pairs timed user inputs with explicit execution and preservation criteria, balanced across five durations.

sections.body: Each model is run three times per test case, and scores are averaged across five equal-weight duration strata. Avatar tasks add a bonus of 5 for systems that support custom avatars, so their Overall can reach 105. In instruction editing, Vidu S2 Editing reaches Overall 45.43 with Edit Success 57.20, while JoyAI-Video-Edit reaches Preservation 83.33. In reference editing, the highest Edit Success is 15.00. Quality, at up to 22.99, and Stability, at up to 13.94, remain low even for the highest-scoring editing systems.
sections.heading: System Evaluation
sections.headline: Evaluating 38 models across five tasks, Vidu S2 Editing ranks first in both editing tasks.

sections.body: The session starts with reference A, a red velvet cape, switches to reference B, a gold satin cape, at 10 s, and requests removal at 20 s. Both sampled B-phase outputs keep the scene of the latest source frame. However, they retain the original grey cape rather than the requested gold satin appearance. The figure pairs source and output frames at recorded session times. Benchmark coverage combines synthetic portraits and speech, controlled acoustic variations and licensed source videos. The authors name broader identities, environments, global resets and selective restoration during active edits as future extensions.
sections.heading: Analysis and Qualitative Results
sections.headline: A recorded reference-editing session shows retained source content but no adoption of the requested gold satin cape.

sections.body: This section groups related work into efficient streaming generators, memory methods for changing controls, avatar systems, streaming editors and evaluation protocols. The authors describe existing benchmarks as examining complementary aspects of these requirements. Full-Duplex-Bench and VideoFDB address conversational behavior, while WBench-Editing and LongV2VBench address editing over changing or long sources. StreamAV-Bench covers interactive updates and state retention. The section argues that StreamEval combines task execution, state consistency and visual fidelity in one assessment.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior benchmarks each cover part of streaming video, leaving no single protocol for all five StreamEval task types.

sections.body: The conclusion states that StreamEval unifies five interactive tasks in 300 scripted cases tied to explicit execution and state-preservation requirements. Evaluation of 38 models shows complementary strengths across tasks, while online action following and reference-based editing remain difficult. The authors name improving request execution alongside visual fidelity and state continuity as a direction for model design. They propose collecting human pairwise judgments and checking their agreement with the task-specific rubric. The stated goal is omni-modal real-time interactive applications.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Request execution and reference-based editing remain challenging, with the highest reference Edit Success at 15.00.

sections.body: The appendix lists the StreamEval team, including Jungang Li, Ziqi Huang, Tian Ye, Jun Zhu and others. It states that author order does not reflect relative contributions. The acknowledgments thank ShengShu Technology for computational resources. They also name partner institutions: Tsinghua University, NVIDIA, Carnegie Mellon University, the University of California, Berkeley, Princeton University, the National University of Singapore, and Reactor.
